metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully opened About Profiles page showing two profiles: 'default-release' (current default) and 'default' (with Rename/Remove/Set as default buttons visible).
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open About Profiles via Help menu, then interact with profile management UI buttons.
metadata.explanation: Chained task: open About Profiles (proven in source trajectory), then click Rename on the 'default' profile and enter 'backup'. Thunderbird immediately writes the name change to profiles.ini. The vm_command_line getter reads profiles.ini and the custom metric uses regex to confirm 'Name=backup' is present (exact match) and 'Name=default' is absent (exact match, excludes 'default-release'). Initial state has 'Name=default' present and 'Name=backup' absent, so it scores 0.0 satisfying the negative-control requirement.

scoring_breakdown.profile_renamed: 1.0 - profiles.ini has Name=backup and no exact Name=default entry

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads /home/user/.thunderbird/profiles.ini via vm_command_line, which is the authoritative file Thunderbird updates when a profile is renamed.
Metric correctly handles type='rule' expected parameter: directly accesses expected.get('new_profile_name') and expected.get('old_profile_name') without any 'rules' wrapper — correct pattern.
Regex logic uses exact-line anchoring (^Name=<name>\s*$, MULTILINE) to distinguish 'default' from 'default-release', correctly allowing the latter to remain while requiring the former to disappear.
Checks both that 'Name=backup' is present AND that 'Name=default' is absent, fully verifying the rename operation.
File-based getter requires no postconfig — profiles.ini persists on disk after the UI rename action.
Negative control is satisfied: initial state has Name=default (returns 0.0) and no Name=backup, so an untouched environment scores 0.0.
Full instruction coverage: 'rename default to backup' is the only verifiable end-state requirement; opening the profile manager is a means, not an independently verifiable goal.
